questions: What specific operation constitutes an “adjustment of elements between them” – can we swap any number of elements, replace elements, or move elements without removal?
Are the elements being adjusted required to stay in the same order within each list after the adjustment, or can their relative order change arbitrarily?
Must the total number of elements in each list remain unchanged after adjustments, or are we allowed to add or remove elements from either list?
Do the lists contain only integers, or are other numeric types (floats, Decimals) permitted, and how should non‑integer values be treated regarding evenness?
Is an element considered “even” only if it is an integer divisible by 2, or should numbers like 4.0 or 2.5 be interpreted as even or not?
When determining feasibility, should we consider the possibility of performing multiple sequential adjustments, or is a single simultaneous redistribution of elements the only allowed scenario?
Should the function treat duplicate values as distinct elements (i.e., each occurrence can be moved independently), or are duplicates considered indistinguishable?
What exact string values should be returned for success and failure – must they be uppercase "YES"/"NO" with no surrounding whitespace or newline characters?
answers: Adjustment means swapping elements between the two lists (the same operation as the original "exchange") -- not moving, replacing, or removing elements.
Order does not matter -- the solution only counts parities of elements and is unaffected by order.
Yes, list lengths stay unchanged since elements are swapped one-for-one between the lists, not added or removed.
Not applicable -- inputs are lists of integers only, per the reference solution.
Not applicable -- evenness is standard integer parity (n % 2 == 0); no floats are considered.
Any number of swaps are allowed; feasibility is checked as an aggregate count comparison, not as a sequence of discrete steps.
Not applicable -- each occurrence is simply counted independently by parity; duplicate values are treated the same as any other value.
Not applicable -- must return exactly "YES" or "NO", uppercase, with no extra whitespace.
